beats.vo: Your towel grows a film of bacteria.
beats.visual: Filmed-looking macro of cotton terry under a window key light; slow slide, push between the loops from 0.8 s; a pale teal film is revealed in the base weave on 'film'.

beats.vo: The claim: use disposable towels for ideal skin. Let's check the receipt.
screen: CLAIM: disposable towels for ideal skin
beats.visual: The receipt strip prints the claim in Courier Prime, a printer tick on each word. A hand of mid-brown skin tone lifts the towel (touch motivates the move).

beats.vo: Line one. Does that film really form? One study gave new cotton towels to twenty-six households.
beats.visual: Receipt line 1 prints. Twenty-six small house icons tick onto the strip one after another, each with a folded white towel. Lateral slide along the row.

beats.vo: Six months of normal home use. Every two months, they tested the towels.
beats.visual: A calendar strip prints with three tick marks at months 2, 4 and 6; a towel is lifted from a basket at each tick. Slow lateral slide follows the ticks.

beats.vo: By month two, the towels smelled and looked dull. Under a microscope: biofilm.
beats.visual: Side-by-side towels, bright white and dull grey. A macro push-in on the weave of the dull one, down to fibre scale: pale teal film sits between the loops. Motivated macro push on the word biofilm.

beats.vo: Live bacteria counts were highest at month six. The film kept building.
beats.visual: A simple bar strip prints three bars for months 2, 4 and 6; the last bar rises tallest in Verified Teal. Locked-off, the bar grows on the word highest.
A Verified Teal HOLDS UP stamp lands on line 1 with a soft printer tick. Static.

beats.vo: Line two. Is it your own skin's bacteria? Mostly not. Staph, a common skin bacterium, was typically well under one percent.
beats.visual: Receipt line 2 prints. Macro slide across a forearm of deep brown skin, then a split frame: a skin-microbe swatch beside a towel-microbe swatch, clearly different shapes. A tiny Staph sliver on the towel side. Slow lateral slide.

beats.vo: The authors think bacteria that suit towel fibres move in and settle.
beats.visual: Macro of cotton loops, small teal shapes settle into the gaps between fibres and stay. Slow hold.

beats.vo: Line three. Does the film hurt your skin? The study never looked at anyone's skin health or infections.
beats.visual: Receipt line 3 prints. A person of light-olive skin dries their cheek with a towel in close-up; a Slate dashed outline marks the cheek with a question mark. Camera drifts laterally with the towel pat.

beats.vo: And disposable towels? This study didn't test those either.
beats.visual: Plain unlabelled paper towels beside a cotton towel; both stay unbranded. The receipt prints 'not tested' in Slate. Slow push-in.

beats.vo: What dermatologists do say: never share towels. And pat your skin dry with a clean one.
beats.visual: Two towels hang on separate hooks; a receipt strip prints 'never share' and 'pat dry, clean towel'. Static medium shot.
Receipt total line prints; a Slate UNKNOWN stamp lands in Courier Prime. Printer tick, hold 1 s stillness.

beats.vo: The film is real. Harm to your skin? Unproven. Disposable towels? Not tested. Dermatologists say clean, and not shared.
beats.visual: Calm pull-back from a towel macro to the whole receipt strip; the one-line summary prints.

beats.vo: A dermatologist can check your skin.
beats.visual: Gentle lateral slide across a range of skin tones, final frame on the end-card text. Hold 1.8 s.

end_card.text: Receipt total: UNKNOWN · A film of bacteria does grow on towels in daily use. Harm to your skin? Unproven. Disposable towels? Not tested. Dermatologists say: clean, and not shared. Education, not medical advice.
